Subject: SLA template — request for credit cap & uptime floor change

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the draft SLA. Procurement has a couple of constraints we need addressed before legal will proceed: specifically, we need an uptime commitment of 99.95% for our production endpoints and a hard monthly credit cap (invoice-creditable) of 15% of our monthly invoice for the first 12 months.

Two quick asks so we can move this internally:
- Can you confirm you can commit to 99.95% for production (we run dedicated critical services)?
- Can the monthly service credit be expressed as an invoice credit (not service credit) and capped at 15% for year one?

If you can send an updated SLA (redlines are fine) and an example calculation for a typical incident, procurement will fast-track the signature. We're on a procurement timeline and would like to close within two weeks if possible.

Thanks — appreciate you moving quickly on this.

Sara Mills

Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Acme SLA request — proposal options

All — quick internal brainstorm before we reply to Acme. Key constraints and recommended counterproposal:

- Feasibility: 99.95% is achievable for Dedicated but not guaranteed on Hosted during maintenance/bursty events.
- Credits: we should avoid a permanent 15% invoice cap on Hosted; propose a tiered approach.

Recommended counterproposal (single combined offer to present to Acme):
1) Dedicated Production: 99.95% uptime SLA, monthly invoice-credit cap of 20%, per-incident cap of 10% of month's bill.
2) Hosted Production: 99.9% uptime SLA, monthly invoice-credit cap of 15%, per-incident cap of 7.5% of month's bill.
3) Latency: commit P95 generation latency < 300ms for typical production workloads, with an exclusion for scheduled maintenance and force-majeure.
4) Reporting: provide monthly uptime report + raw metrics on demand and a 30-day pilot for Dedicated pool if Acme wants to validate.

If Acme insists on a 15% invoice cap for Dedicated, push for a 12-month term limit (i.e., 15% capped for first year, then revert). Also propose a short SLA review at 6 months.

Markus — can you confirm that the per-incident calculation below is acceptable to Finance? (monthly bill * minutes of downtime above threshold / total minutes in month) — we'll include a worked example.

Tessa — if you're comfortable with that framing, I'll draft the external reply.

-Jordan

Subject: Re: SLA template — request for credit cap & uptime floor change

Hi Sara / Acme procurement team,

Appreciate the clarity on timeline. After internal review, here is a concise counterproposal that balances your reliability needs with a defensible credit framework:

Proposal summary (single-document counter):
- Dedicated Production: 99.95% uptime SLA. Monthly invoice-credit cap = 20% of monthly invoice; per-incident invoice-credit cap = 10% of monthly invoice.
- Hosted Production: 99.9% uptime SLA. Monthly invoice-credit cap = 15% of monthly invoice; per-incident cap = 7.5%.
- Invoice credits: agreed — credits will be issued as invoice credits applied to the next billing cycle.
- Calculation: credits are computed proportionally based on minutes of downtime beyond the SLA period (worked example attached).
- Latency: P95 generation latency SLA target of < 300ms for typical request shapes; see exclusions for scheduled maintenance and customer-caused degradation in Section 4.
- Reporting & validation: we will provide a monthly uptime report, and raw metrics can be made available under NDAs / secure link on request.
- Pilot option: 30-day Dedicated pilot to validate 99.95% availability before signing — optional and charged at a reduced pilot rate.

I've attached the updated SLA draft (Acme_SLA_Draft_v2.pdf) and our last 12 months' uptime summary for your review (uptime-history-nov-to-oct.csv). If this looks close, please have your legal team send redlines; otherwise we can hop on a quick call to walk through specifics.

Next steps:
1) Procurement: confirm whether the pilot is required.
2) Legal: return redlines to elliot_price@redwood.ai.
3) Ops: if pilot is wanted, let us know target start date; Jordan will coordinate capacity.

Thanks — aiming to keep this moving so we can meet your two-week window.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Tessa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the options. A few clarifying items from procurement/legal before we proceed:

1) Calculation example: can you include a worked example showing a 2-hour incident in a 30-day month and how the invoice credit numbers would look for both Dedicated and Hosted?
2) Invoice credit mechanics: procurement prefers credits applied to invoices (confirmed) and prefers language that credits are the exclusive remedy for availability failures. Please have legal propose that phrasing.
3) Per-incident vs monthly cap: procurement wants the per-incident cap explicit in the SLA language (we prefer per-incident <= monthly cap).

We'd also like to run the 30-day Dedicated pilot. What would be the earliest available window? Ops is prepared to kick off on short notice but needs a start date to coordinate internal test runs.

If you can get the worked example and a tiny redline on the exclusive remedy language, procurement will be able to get the contract to legal for signature review.

Appreciate the partnership — we want this in place quickly.

Sara
